title: Does Poland allow border guards to shoot at migrants? Here's what the law says
summary:
Border officers could already use firearms in self-defense before the amendment became law.
It does not allow the indiscriminate use of firearms, although human rights organizations have warned it could lead to excessive force against migrants and weaken accountability for border officers.
In mid-2026, social media users claimed that Poland had passed legislation allowing its border patrol guards to shoot at migrants.
That year, Poland passed amendments to an existing law, allowing border security to use firearms in specific situations.
The amendments do not state that border officers can attack migrants, though human rights groups argue the language gives undue license to border security forces.

title: Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US
summary:
Immigration has always been central to Donald Trump's message.
Some of his first-term ambitions to stem the flow of would-be immigrants were constrained by the courts.
He promised a closed border and mass deportations in his successful 2024 campaign - and few can deny that he's delivered on both.
But even among those who voted for a tougher stance, there is a concern that the crackdown has gone too far.
His signature policy has played out in five key ways.

title: Thugs smash windows and spray paint graffiti on dozens of homes where asylum seekers are believed to stay in anti-HMO attacks leaving families fearing for their safety
summary:
Families have been left fearing for their safety after thugs started smashing windows and spray-painting homes suspected of housing asylum seekers.
Masked thugs have smashed windows, vandalised cars and sprayed 'No HMO' graffiti to hound asylum seekers but in many cases have inadvertently damaged non-HMO homes belonging to long-term residents.
HMOs are increasingly used by the Government and private contractors to house asylum seekers and migrant workers as an alternative to asylum hotels.
Police and council chiefs have vowed to crack down on the suspected racist attacks, which have struck the working-class area of Salford.
The violence comes amid wider tensions over asylum accommodation following months of anti-immigration demonstrations across Britain, including protests outside hotels housing asylum seekers.
